suggestions.assertion: Primary attribution EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT yields the deterministic route revise_here to S7 for retesting, not progression to the next chapter.
suggestions.reason: This is the one genuine behavioral failure in the without_skill run and it is well-targeted: the baseline blocks progression but overshoots the reroute target, sending the learner to S1/S2 (restart evidence collection from foundation) instead of S7 (same-stage targeted retesting). The assertion correctly distinguishes the two. One clarification would help graders: make explicit whether routing to ANY upstream stage is acceptable or whether S7 specifically is required (i.e. 'stays within the current mastery-verification stage for targeted retesting, rather than restarting at an earlier foundation stage'). The current text already implies S7-specific, which is the stricter and more discriminating reading.

eval_feedback.overall: Five of six expectations pass on behavioral substance even though the baseline uses its own field names (version_mismatch/blocking vs update_status=version_conflict; boolean quality_indicators vs not_executed/unknown tokens). The single failure — rerouting to S1/S2 instead of S7 — is a real, discriminating behavioral gap, not merely a schema difference. Consider stating explicitly that S7 (not any upstream stage) is the required reroute target.
